finding.claim: On a big5 connection charset, a Buffer parameter containing a lead byte in 0xFA-0xFE followed by 0x5C causes the client to copy the pair verbatim without escaping, while the server treats the lead as a single byte and the 0x5C as an escape. A following quote then closes the string literal, enabling SQL injection. The server-side big5 lead range is unverified.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled bytes in a Buffer parameter passed to query/execute (e.g. [buf] for a ? placeholder) on a connection with big5 charset
finding.sink: writeBufferEscapeMb emitting _BINARY '...' literal bytes to the server, which parses the SQL with big5 lexing

trace.note: Buffer values are detected and written as _BINARY literal
Raw bytes go to writeBufferEscape with no hex encoding
big5 charset selects writeBufferEscapeMb with the big5 recognizer
big5 isHead accepts 0xA1-0xFE, wider than the believed server range 0xA1-0xF9
Head and trail copied verbatim with no escape inserted
Following quote byte is escaped as backslash-quote

finding.guards_checked: NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES branch at packet-output-stream.js:684 not taken in default mode; Buffer parameters are not hex-encoded; no server-side validation of the byte sequence. Server big5 lead range (believed 0xA1-0xF9 per MySQL/MariaDB ctype-big5.c) could not be verified: WebSearch permission was denied and no local test covers big5.
